note.title: Present tense
note.overview: This lesson contains 52 enabled questions. It teaches Present tense through explicit translation, recall, grammar and application tasks.
learningGoals: Recall the core language for Present tense.
Identify the task direction before writing.
Explain errors by naming the article, subject, tense, auxiliary, agreement or negative rule.
Use the material in a short controlled sentence.
mustMemoriseRules: Identify the subject before choosing a present-tense ending.
aller, avoir and être are irregular and must be memorised.
Regular -er endings: e, es, e, ons, ez, ent.
Regular -ir endings: is, is, it, issons, issez, issent.
Regular -re endings: s, s, no ending, ons, ez, ent.
Negatives wrap around the finite verb.

workedExamples.prompt: Write the « je » form in the aller column.
workedExamples.why: The source conjugation table gives je → vais for aller. The subject decides the written ending.

workedExamples.prompt: Write the « tu » form in the aller column.
workedExamples.why: The source conjugation table gives tu → vas for aller. The subject decides the written ending.

workedExamples.prompt: Write the « il / elle / on » form in the aller column.
workedExamples.why: The source conjugation table gives il / elle / on → va for aller. The subject decides the written ending.

workedExamples.prompt: Write the « nous » form in the aller column.
workedExamples.why: The source conjugation table gives nous → allons for aller. The subject decides the written ending.

workedExamples.prompt: Write the « vous » form in the aller column.
workedExamples.why: The source conjugation table gives vous → allez for aller. The subject decides the written ending.

commonMistakes: Choosing an ending before identifying the subject.
Do not change a correct answer into an error just because the learner also wrote the subject.
A small article or ending can change the grammar even when the main vocabulary is recognisable.
Do not choose an ending by sound alone; several written forms sound alike.
detailedExplanation: This lesson contains 52 enabled questions. It teaches Present tense through explicit translation, recall, grammar and application tasks.

Identify the subject, remove the infinitive ending where appropriate and add the correct present-tense ending. With reflexive verbs, keep the reflexive pronoun matched to the subject and place negatives around the conjugated verb.
examTips: Underline every task requirement before writing and tick each one after it is included.
Build the verb and tense core first; then check articles, negatives and agreement.
Accents should be corrected and displayed, but a missing accent alone does not lose the app mark.
